summary: Regression of an enzyme's turnover number (kcat) for a given substrate, from the protein sequence and the substrate SMILES.
what_it_measures: log10(kcat) in s⁻¹ for an enzyme–substrate pair, standardized (`kcat_standardized`). This is a protein+ligand task: the model sees both the sequence and the reaction's substrate.
assay_method: In-vitro steady-state kinetics compiled and cleaned by CatPred (drawing on BRENDA/SABIO-RK-style sources), with careful de-duplication and out-of-distribution splits.
provenance: From the CatPred kcat benchmark; substrate SMILES are canonicalized and described by the 200 normalized RDKit 2D descriptors of descriptastorus (RDKit2DNormalized), concatenated with the protein embedding.
when_to_use: A core enzyme-kinetics regression testing whether embeddings (plus ligand descriptors) capture catalytic efficiency; central to enzyme selection and engineering.
caveats: kcat spans orders of magnitude and is measurement-noisy; targets are log10 values standardized on the training split, so MAE is in standardized units. Kendall's tau is the primary metric.

citations.authors: Boorla, V. S. & Maranas, C. D.
citations.title: CatPred: a comprehensive framework for deep learning in vitro enzyme kinetic parameters
